diagnostic_definition.calibration_factor: C = sum(x*y)/sum(x^2), where x is molecular RCS and y is measured glued RCS on the candidate window
uncertainty_models: propagated per-bin error with independent altitude bins
perfect positive correlation of every valid altitude bin
stationary lag-correlation model estimated from block-demeaned uncertainty-scaled Level-1 PC residuals
diagnostic_definition.important_boundary_caveat: Productive KFS method v4 still uses the exact measured RCS at one reference bin as X_ref. This window-fit uncertainty diagnostic does not change the productive boundary condition.

interpretation_notes: The existing candidate uncertainty_snr_median is a median bin-wise signal/error diagnostic and is not the same quantity as uncertainty of the fitted molecular scale over the full reference window.
For this measurement the full local Rayleigh window contains substantially more calibration-scale information than the bin-wise SNR alone suggests under the empirical short-range covariance model.

The large separation between independent-bin and fully-correlated limits demonstrates that altitude-bin dependence must remain explicit; the favorable model cannot be selected merely to extend retrieval altitude.

A future R&D path is to compare the current exact noisy-bin X_ref boundary against a window-fitted local boundary estimate at the same center altitude using synthetic truth and contaminated-window cases.
Any productive use of a fitted boundary would change retrieval-method semantics and require a method-version change plus explicit uncertainty propagation.
This evidence does not authorize a higher Rayleigh reference, a hard SNR threshold, productive smoothing, or a 15/20 km support claim.
